data.name: Saksham
data.gender_notes: Saksham is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Saksham is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Saksh' which means 'to witness'. The name Saksham means 'able to see or perceive' and is given to a child who is believed to have the ability to observe and understand the world around them with clarity and wisdom. This name is often given to a child who is expected to be courageous and truthful in their actions and words.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Saksham holds spiritual significance as it is believed to bring the blessings of the God of Sight, Agni, who is the witness of all actions and the purifier of all sins. The name is said to instil in the child a sense of transparency and courage, and the ability to see beyond the physical world.
data.etymology: Saksham belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Able to see or perceive.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saksham total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Saksham holds great importance in Hindu culture as it is considered a quality that a virtuous and honorable person should possess. To witness and understand the world around us and the actions of those around us is a valuable trait, and this name is believed to bestow that quality upon the child. In addition, the name often signifies courage and truthfulness, making it a beloved and esteemed name in Hindu families.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Saksham lies in its implication of having the divine gift of perception and understanding. In Hinduism, it is believed that the ability to truly see and understand the world around us and the actions of others is an essential aspect of spiritual growth. By bestowing the name Saksham upon a child, parents are expressing their hope and belief that the child will develop this valuable quality and use it to navigate the complexities of life with wisdom and discernment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Saksham signifies one who bears witness to the divine within oneself and in the world. It is a reminder to be present and aware in each moment, recognizing the divine spark in all beings.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Saksham was a king of the Vedic period. The name Saksham carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Saksham was a king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, mentioned in the Rigveda.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Saksham continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
